newsitem.title: USA: Separatists fall silent in Texas standoff.
newsitem.headline: Separatists fall silent in Texas standoff.

text.p: Communications with an armed Texas separatist group holed up in a remote mountain compound have stopped, without an agreement to end a four-day standoff, a police spokesman said Wednesday.

Texas Department of Public Safety spokesman Mike Cox said members of the Republic of Texas group had halted telephone negotiations with police for unknown reasons and it was now unclear when or how the siege might end.

Cox said that contrary to an earlier television report, Republic of Texas leader Richard McLaren never formally agreed to surrender to police before putting a halt to the talks. But, he said, negotiators had come close to reaching a deal.
"There was the optimistic feeling they were going to sign an agreement. The agreement has never been signed," he said.

Cox said it had been "a good while" since the separatists, who want Texas to secede from the United States, have spoken to police. "We don't know why. We just simply stopped hearing from him," he said.

The standoff began on Sunday when group members took two hostages in retaliation for the arrest of their security chief. Felony charges with penalties of up to 99 years in prison have been filed against six of the separatists, including McLaren.
